name.text: 01 Question: Lemma vs Inflected Surface Token

questiontext.text: <p>What is the precise definition of a 'lemma' in computational linguistics and lexicography?</p>

answer.text: <p>The canonical, uninflected base form (headword) under which a set of inflected words is conventionally grouped in a dictionary.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. A lemma is the chosen dictionary citation form (e.g., 'write' for 'writes', 'wrote', 'written').</p>

answer.text: <p>The physical ink composition used by a medieval scriptorium.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Lemma is a linguistic and lexicographical concept, not a chemical writing fluid.</p>

answer.text: <p>A software bug that causes a computer program to loop endlessly.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. An endless loop is a software defect, not a lemma.</p>

answer.text: <p>The physical dimension of a parchment leaf measured in millimeters.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Leaf dimension is a codicological measurement, not a linguistic lemma.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>Which set of linguistic categories constitutes the morphological feature bundle for a fully inflected finite verb in historical inflected languages?</p>

answer.text: <p>Person, number, tense, voice, and mood.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Finite verbs are parsed according to person (1st/2nd/3rd), number (singular/plural/dual), tense, voice, and mood.</p>

answer.text: <p>Shelfmark, binding, watermark, and collation formula.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are codicological book-structure terms.</p>

answer.text: <p>Brightness, contrast, saturation, and gamma curve.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are digital imaging raster attributes.</p>

answer.text: <p>Font family, font size, line height, and letter spacing.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. These are typographic and CSS formatting properties.</p>

name.text: 03 Question: TEI Encoding of Linguistic Words

questiontext.text: <p>How does TEI P5 recommend encoding an individual word token with its associated lemma and part-of-speech tag?</p>

answer.text: <p><w lemma="regere" pos="verb">rexit</w></p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. The <w> element encloses the inflected surface token with attributes providing the dictionary lemma and part-of-speech category.</p>

answer.text: <p><choice><orig>regere</orig><reg>rexit</reg></choice></p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. <choice><orig><reg> is used for orthographic regularization, not grammatical lemmatization.</p>

answer.text: <p><teiHeader type="verb" n="rexit"/></p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. teiHeader is the document metadata container, not an inline word element.</p>

answer.text: <p><abbr expan="rexit">regere</abbr></p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. <abbr> and <expan> are for scribal abbreviation expansion, not inflectional parsing.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>Why is automated morphological parsing inherently challenging in inflected historical languages?</p>

answer.text: <p>Because identical surface word forms (homographs) can represent multiple distinct lemmas or grammatical analyses, requiring syntactic and semantic context to disambiguate.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Inflected languages exhibit widespread syncretism and homography, where a single spelling may represent several different cases, genders, or entirely different words.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because historical manuscripts were written in secret cyphers designed to prevent reading.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Premodern literary and archival manuscripts were intended to be read by literate communities.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because computers are fundamentally incapable of processing text written before the year 1900.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Computers process textual data of any era provided character encodings are defined.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because ancient languages had no rules of grammar or syntax.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Classical and historical languages possessed highly rigorous, formalized grammatical systems.</p>

name.text: 05 Question: Role of the Classical Language Toolkit (CLTK)

questiontext.text: <p>What primary function does the Classical Language Toolkit (CLTK) Python library serve in digital humanities research?</p>

answer.text: <p>It provides specialized Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools, tokenizers, lemmatizers, and language models tailored specifically for ancient and medieval languages.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. CLTK is an open-source library providing NLP pipelines for Greek, Latin, Old English, Sanskrit, and dozens of historical languages.</p>

answer.text: <p>It is a hardware device that physically flattens ancient parchment scrolls.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. CLTK is a software library, not a physical conservation machine.</p>

answer.text: <p>It automatically converts historical documents into 3D video games.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. CLTK focuses on computational linguistic text analysis.</p>

answer.text: <p>It replaces university registrars by automatically grading student tuition payments.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. CLTK has no administrative registrar functionality.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>What occurs when a rule-based or dictionary-lookup lemmatizer encounters an 'Out-of-Vocabulary' (OOV) word in a historical text?</p>

answer.text: <p>It fails to assign a lemma, either returning an unknown token flag or defaulting to the surface string, because the form does not exist in its static lexicon.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Static lexicon lookups cannot parse novel spelling variants, dialectal forms, or rare compound words not previously catalogued in the dictionary.</p>

answer.text: <p>It immediately deletes the entire computer operating system.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Software graceful degradation returns null or unknown flags, not system deletion.</p>

answer.text: <p>It contacts the author of the manuscript via email for clarification.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Authors of historical manuscripts are deceased.</p>

answer.text: <p>It converts all adjacent words into capital letters.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. OOV handling does not alter casing of surrounding tokens.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>In a Universal Dependencies (UD) syntactic treebank, what do nodes and directed edges represent?</p>

answer.text: <p>Nodes represent individual words (tokens), and directed edges represent grammatical dependency relations pointing from a syntactic head to its dependent modifier.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Dependency grammar structures sentences as rooted trees where words connect via labeled grammatical relations (e.g. subject, object, modifier) directed from heads to dependents.</p>

answer.text: <p>Nodes represent library buildings, and edges represent delivery truck routes.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. That describes a physical logistical network, not a syntactic treebank.</p>

answer.text: <p>Nodes represent punctuation marks, and edges represent paper thickness.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Dependency trees model the grammatical architecture of human language.</p>

answer.text: <p>Nodes represent computer memory addresses, and edges represent electric current.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. That describes computer hardware architecture, not linguistic syntax.</p>

name.text: 08 Question: AI Hallucinations in Morphological Parsing

questiontext.text: <p>What is a common failure mode when asking a general-purpose commercial LLM to lemmatize historical Greek or Latin poetry?</p>

answer.text: <p>Hallucinating modern language roots, inventing non-existent dictionary headwords, or confabulating grammatical genders to fit modern linguistic intuitions.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Without domain-specific grounding, general LLMs frequently project modern vocabulary or invent plausible-sounding but fictitious classical lemmas.</p>

answer.text: <p>Outputting responses entirely in binary Morse code.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. LLMs respond in natural language or requested structured formats.</p>

answer.text: <p>Crashing the web browser due to excessive file size.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Text parsing outputs are small text objects that do not crash browsers.</p>

answer.text: <p>Refusing to parse words that have more than six letters.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Models have no arbitrary character length restrictions on words.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>Why is high-quality lemmatization indispensable for large-scale corpus analysis and digital text indexing?</p>

answer.text: <p>It collapses all inflected surface variants into a single conceptual index, enabling researchers to search and model vocabulary regardless of grammatical endings.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Lemmatization enables accurate frequency analysis, concordances, topic modeling, and stylometric search across inflected languages.</p>

answer.text: <p>It prevents readers from copying text out of a PDF document.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Lemmatization is an analytical enhancement, not digital rights management (DRM).</p>

answer.text: <p>It reduces the physical weight of printed books in libraries.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital data processing does not alter the physical mass of paper codices.</p>

answer.text: <p>It automatically translates the entire text into modern emoji pictograms.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Lemmatization preserves scholarly linguistic rigor.</p>

name.text: 10 Question: Human-in-the-Loop Verification of Linguistic Data

questiontext.text: <p>In a digital scholarly critical edition, why must automated linguistic annotations undergo human expert review?</p>

answer.text: <p>Because grammatical interpretation often reflects subtle theological, philosophical, or literary arguments that probabilistic algorithms cannot adjudicate authoritatively.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. High-level syntactic and morphological decisions often define the core interpretive contribution of a scholarly edition, requiring expert human adjudication.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because university regulations forbid the use of any software written after 1995.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Universities actively support modern technological research.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because automated taggers always produce 0% accuracy on every language.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Modern taggers often achieve 85-95% accuracy, but the remaining errors are critical philological cruxes.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because XML files become unreadable by web browsers if created by a computer script.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Browsers parse XML regardless of whether it was typed by hand or generated by a script.</p>
